1.sofaString: 115	Pt, ********** ***** (***. Baby/***** ***********), is a 12 day-old female with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, referred by ***** ******, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient's mother, ***** **** *******, patient's father, ****** *****, and review of the medical records. SW spent approximately 45 minutes of face-to-face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  Pt, **********, was born here at ****** and has not yet left the hospital. Her parents and older brother reside with the maternal grandmother and grandfather in ******, *******. They reside at *** ****** **** *****, ******, ** *****. They live in * 3-bedroom apartment with central heating and a/c.  They change the air filter monthly. They have city water. There is no smoking in the home.  There are no pets in the home.      Demographics:  Mother:  ***** **** *******  DOB:  **/**/****  Language: English, *******  Education Level: 11th Grade  Employment:  Stay at home mom  Phone:  ***-***-****     Father:  ****** *****  ***:  **/**/****  Language: English, *******  Education Level: GED  Employment:  Carpet Installer with ***** of Floors  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  ********* ******-****- 5      Social History and Support Systems:  **********'s family is currently residing with the maternal grandparents. Parents have been in a relationship for 1.5 years. Prior to moving a few weeks ago they were residing in ********, **.  Mom is from ****** **** and dad is from Kissimmee. They have a significant amount of local family support. **********'s paternal grandmother resides in Kissimmee. There are also several maternal aunts living in ******. Family has significant social support through their family.  Mom will be **********'s primary caregiver post-transplant. Since dad plans to return to work, the maternal grandmother, ***** *******, will be the secondary caregiver to assist mom and ********** if needed.  Mom disclosed that ***********'s brother, *********, is already struggling to adjust to the situation. He has told the parents that they **** the baby more than him and has been acting out in school. They would like him to start in counseling. SW will provide family with a list of in-network counselors near the family's home.  Parents deny any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.     Course of illness:     ********** was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome prenatally. She was sent to ****** for delivery. She was scheduled to undergo a *******/Sano procedure on **/** but due to having runs of SVT requiring defibrillation and adenosine as well as the TEE showing worsening moderate to severe tricuspid valve regurgitation the surgery was cancelled. She was emergently listed status 1A for heart transplant.     Financial situation:  The family does not have an income at this time. A few weeks ago, dad started a job as a carpet installer with ***** of Floors. Due to infant's medical condition, he has been unable to work. He does not have any paid time off nor is he eligible for FMLA. He plans to return to work as soon as possible. The family does receive WIC and **********. At this time, they are not required to pay **** at the grandparent's home but plan to do so when dad is able to return to work. Due to recent financial constraints, mom's phone was turned off. The only working phone for the family is the father's cell. They have not yet applied for social security disability. SW will contact ******* and ask them to assist the family with initiating application. SW also provided family with information on ****. Dad did state that a family member was starting a ******** page for the family.  ********** is covered by ******** Medicaid. This will cover all medical expenses at 100%.           The family has one vehicle. They deny that transportation will be a barrier for the family. However, SW met with family again the day after interview and dad was having trouble getting home due to having a blown tire and not having the financial means to have tire repaired.      Family History:  Mom has a significant history of domestic violence, DCF, and law enforcement involvement with the father of her older child. Mom reports that there was ongoing violence between her and the father, both as ************. There was one instance where they were both arrested but charges were dropped by both parties. DCF was involved several times. This was in *** ****. There has been no contact between her and *********'s father since ***** of this year. ***** chose to move away to limit his involvement.   They deny any significant mental health history.     Adherence:  There are no documented concerns for adherence.      Assessment and recommendations:  Both parents verbalized willingness to move forward with transplant. SW is unsure about the family's understanding of the risks/benefits as well as the transplant process. This could likely be due to the family being given all of this information in a very short amount of time. They would benefit from ongoing education. The family's lack of income as well as mom's history of being both a perpetrator and victim of domestic violence is concerning. SW will continue to work with family and provide support during hospitalization.
